title: Pope St. Eusebius (31º): Biography, Pontificate & Legacy
sourceNotes: Roman citizen of Greek descent. Banished by Emperor Maxentius and died in exile; feast day 17 August.

title: Pope St. Miltiades (Melchiades) (32º): Lateran Council — Complete Guide
sourceNotes: Roman citizen of Berber descent. Feast day 10 January. First pope after the end of the persecution of Christians through the Edict of Milan(313), issued by Emperor Constantine I. Presided over the Lateran Council of 313.

title: Pope St. Sylvester I (33º): Biography, Pontificate & Legacy
birthPlace: Sant'Angelo a Scala, Italy, Roman Empire
sourceNotes: Roman citizen. Feast day 31 December. Also revered as a saint in Eastern Christianity, with a feast day of 2 January. Pope during the First Council of Nicaea(325), the first ecumenical council. Under him were built: the Archbasilica of Saint John Lateran, the Santa Croce in Gerusalemme, and the Old St. Peter's Basilica. Stated to be the recipient of the Donation of Constantine, which was later shown to be a forgery.

title: Pope St. Mark (34º): Martyrdom & Sainthood — Complete Guide
sourceNotes: Roman citizen. Feast day 7 October. Compiled stories of martyrs and bishops before his time. May have founded two churches in the area of Rome: Church of San Marco and a church at the Catacomb of Balbina, a cemetery.

title: Pope St. Julius I (35º): Biography, Pontificate & Legacy
sourceNotes: Roman citizen. Feast day 12 April. He was involved in the Arian controversy, supporting Athanasius of Alexandria.

title: Pope Liberius (36º): Biography, Pontificate & Legacy
sourceNotes: Roman citizen. Banished by the Arian-leaning Emperor Constantius II and later yielding to him. Earliest pope not canonized by the Latin Church. Revered as a saint in Eastern Christianity, with a feast day of 27 August.

title: Pope St. Damasus I (37º): Biography, Pontificate & Legacy
sourceNotes: Roman citizen. First pope from modern-day Portugal. Feast day 11 December. Patron of Jerome, commissioned the Vulgate translation of the Bible. Pope during the First Council of Constantinople(381), the second ecumenical council, and the Council of Rome(382). First pope to be the official head of the church after Emperor Gratian abdicated the title of Pontifex Maximus.

title: Pope St. Siricius (38º): Biography, Pontificate & Legacy
sourceNotes: Roman citizen. Feast day 26 November. His famous letters—the earliest surviving texts of papal decretals—were focused particularly on religious discipline and include decisions on baptism, consecration, ordination, penance, and continence. Siricius's important decretal of 386 (written to Bishop Himerius of Tarragona), commanding celibacy for priests, was the first decree on this subject.

title: Pope St. Anastasius I (39º): Biography, Pontificate & Legacy
sourceNotes: Roman citizen. Feast day 19 December. Instructed priests to stand and bow their heads as they read from the Gospels.

title: Pope St. Innocent I (40º): Biography, Pontificate & Legacy
sourceNotes: Roman citizen. Feast day 12 March. Rome was sacked by the Visigoths under King Alaric I(410).

title: Pope St. Zosimus (41º): Biography, Pontificate & Legacy
sourceNotes: Roman citizen of Greek descent. Feast day 27 December.

title: Pope St. Boniface I (42º): Biography, Pontificate & Legacy
sourceNotes: Roman citizen. Feast day 25 October.

title: Pope St. Celestine I (43º): Biography, Pontificate & Legacy
sourceNotes: Roman citizen. Feast day 27 July. Also revered as a saint in Eastern Christianity, with a feast day of 8 April. Pope during the Council of Ephesus(431), the third ecumenical council recognized by the Catholic, Eastern Orthodox, and Oriental Orthodox churches.

title: Pope St. Sixtus III (44º): Biography, Pontificate & Legacy
sourceNotes: Roman citizen. Feast day 28 March.

title: Pope St. Leo I the Great (45º): Attila, Chalcedon & Papal Authority
sourceNotes: Roman citizen. Feast day 10 November. Convinced Attila the Hun to turn back his invasion of Italy. Convinced the Vandals to spare the lives of the citizenry of Rome during their sack of the city. Wrote the Tome, which was instrumental in the Council of Chalcedon(451) and in defining the hypostatic union. Also revered as a saint in Eastern Christianity, with a feast day of 18 February.

title: Pope St. Hilarius (46º): Biography, Pontificate & Legacy
sourceNotes: Roman citizen. Feast day 28 February.

title: Pope St. Simplicius (47º): Biography, Pontificate & Legacy
sourceNotes: Roman citizen, later a subject of the Kingdom of Italy. Feast day 10 March. Pope during the collapse of the Western Roman Empire in 476 and subsequent overtaking of Rome and Italy in general by King Odoacer.

title: Pope St. Felix III (48º): Biography, Pontificate & Legacy
sourceNotes: Roman citizen, later a subject of the Kingdom of Italy. Feast day 1 March. Sometimes called Felix II. Great-great-grandfather of Gregory I.

title: Pope St. Gelasius I (49º): Biography, Pontificate & Legacy
sourceNotes: Roman citizen of Berber descent, later a subject of the(Ostrogothic) Kingdom of Italy; last pope to have been born on the continent of Africa. Feast day 21 November. First pope called the Vicarius Christi(Vicar of Christ).

title: Pope Anastasius II (50º): Biography, Pontificate & Legacy
sourceNotes: Roman citizen of Greek descent, later a subject of the(Ostrogothic) Kingdom of Italy. Tried to end the Acacian schism, but it resulted in the Laurentian schism. Earliest pope not canonized by either the Latin Church or the Eastern Church.

title: Pope St. Symmachus (51º): Biography, Pontificate & Legacy
sourceNotes: Roman citizen, later a subject of the(Ostrogothic) Kingdom of Italy. Feast day 19 July.

title: Pope St. Hormisdas (52º): Biography, Pontificate & Legacy
sourceNotes: Roman citizen, later a subject of the(Ostrogothic) Kingdom of Italy. Feast day 6 August. Father of Silverius. Acacian schism.

title: Pope St. John I (53º): Biography, Pontificate & Legacy
sourceNotes: Roman citizen, later a subject of the(Ostrogothic) Kingdom of Italy. Feast day 18 May. Theoderic had John arrested on the suspicion of having conspired with Emperor Justin. John was imprisoned at Ravenna, where he died of neglect and ill treatment.

title: Pope St. Felix IV (54º): Biography, Pontificate & Legacy
sourceNotes: Subject of the(Ostrogothic) Kingdom of Italy of Roman descent. Feast day 30 January. Sometimes called Felix III. Built Santi Cosma e Damiano.

title: Pope Boniface II (55º): Martyrdom & Sainthood — Complete Guide
sourceNotes: Ostrogoth; first Germanic pope. Subject of the(Ostrogothic) Kingdom of Italy. Changed the method of numbering the years in the Julian calendar from Anno Martyrum to Anno Domini.

title: Pope John II (56º): Biography, Pontificate & Legacy
sourceNotes: Roman citizen, later a subject of the(Ostrogothic) Kingdom of Italy. First pope not to use his personal name (Mercurius), as it was associated with the Roman god Mercury.

title: Pope St. Agapetus I (57º): Biography, Pontificate & Legacy
sourceNotes: Subject of the(Ostrogothic) Kingdom of Italy of Roman descent. Feast days 22 April and 20 September. Also revered as a saint in Eastern Christianity, with a feast day of 17 April.

title: Pope St. Silverius (58º): Biography, Pontificate & Legacy
sourceNotes: Subject of the(Ostrogothic) Kingdom of Italy of Roman descent. Exiled; feast day 20 June. Son of Hormisdas.

title: Pope Vigilius (59º): Biography, Pontificate & Legacy
sourceNotes: Subject of the(Ostrogothic) Kingdom of Italy, later a(Eastern) Roman citizen. Was of Roman ethnicity. Pope during the Second Council of Constantinople(553), the fifth ecumenical council recognized by the Catholic and Eastern Orthodox churches.

title: Pope Pelagius I (60º): Biography, Pontificate & Legacy
sourceNotes: Subject of the(Ostrogothic) Kingdom of Italy, later a(Eastern) Roman citizen. Was of Roman ethnicity. Credited with the construction of the basilica of Santi Apostoli.
